body_markdown:
Zite, built by the company behind Fillout, is an AI app builder known for unlimited app users and visual workflow editing. However, builders seeking mobile app capabilities, source code ownership, or flexible AI-assisted development workflows may want to explore alternatives.[Floot](https://floot.com/) and other platforms offer different approaches to building and publishing functional applications.


Choosing the right alternative depends on your requirements for databases, authentication, hosting, mobile publishing, and code portability. According to Gartner research, the low-code development technologies market is projected to reach[$58.2 billion by 2029](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/7146430) . This guide compares eight Zite alternatives for founders, operators, and teams planning to build applications in 2027.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **AI assistant integration** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) enables application building through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Available building operations depend on connector permissions and client capabilities.
- **Managed full-stack infrastructure** : Floot includes[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) such as PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, hosting, and email, reducing the need to configure separate backend services.
- **Mobile app development** : Floot supports[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) on every plan: 2 per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited on Power. Floot handles iOS and Android builds without requiring local development tools. App-store publishing requires developer accounts and approval.
- **Code ownership and portability** : Floot users own their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan. Paid plans provide[project code downloads](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) , allowing users to move toward independently managed infrastructure.
- **Flexible pricing structure** : Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) with 100 daily building actions and a starter hosting allowance. Paid plans provide higher action limits, monthly AI credits, and hosting allowances, with usage-based hosting costs beyond the included amounts.


## **Understanding AI App Building Platforms**


AI app building platforms allow people to create applications using natural-language prompts, visual editors, or connected AI development tools. They differ in how they handle databases, authentication, hosting, integrations, and code ownership. Zite emphasizes business workflow applications with unlimited users, while Floot combines an MCP connector with managed full-stack infrastructure. When comparing platforms, consider these requirements:


- **AI-powered development** : Natural-language prompts help generate application interfaces, backend logic, and workflows. Floot supports[building through AI assistants](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) using its connector.
- **Database management** : Applications storing customer records, transactions, or user information need persistent data storage. Floot provides a[managed PostgreSQL database](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) .
- **User authentication** : Applications with private information or multiple user roles need secure sign-up, login, and access controls.
- **Hosting and deployment** : Applications need reliable hosting, live URLs, and domain management. Floot provides[managed hosting](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/hosting) with usage-based billing.
- **Mobile capabilities** : Some platforms produce web applications, while others support native mobile development, installable web apps, or mobile project exports.
- **Code portability** : Source code access affects long-term flexibility. Floot's[self-hosting documentation](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) explains how exported projects can be moved to independent infrastructure.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions.


Rather than replacing existing AI coding tools, Floot works alongside them. It provides hosting, databases, authentication, file storage, and other backend services needed to run working applications.


### **Primary Focus**


Floot serves non-technical founders, business owners, and operators building internal tools, client portals, booking systems, CRMs, and customer-facing web or mobile applications. It is particularly relevant for users who want to work through their existing AI assistants while relying on managed infrastructure for backend operations.


### **Key Capabilities**


Floot provides several core capabilities that support full-stack application development:


- **MCP connector for AI assistants** : Build through supported Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and compatible MCP workflows without learning a separate development interface.
- **Full-stack infrastructure included** : Managed PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting.
- **Mobile app conversion** : Generate installable iOS and Android builds on Free, Pro, and Power, with monthly build limits determined by the selected plan.
- **Code ownership on every plan** : Users own their code, data, and intellectual property, with complete project ZIP downloads available on paid plans.
- **SEO and discoverability tools** : Server-side pre-rendering, sitemap generation, and page metadata settings.


### **Production-Ready Features**


Floot includes managed PostgreSQL databases with SQL access, a browser-based table view, and database export capabilities. Authentication supports email/password login and options for social authentication, including Google and Microsoft OAuth. File storage provides managed uploads and CDN-backed delivery.


[Scheduled tasks](https://floot.com/blog/how-to-schedule-backend-tasks-without-cron-jobs) support recurring backend operations such as daily reports, data synchronization, and cleanup workflows. These jobs run in published applications on eligible paid plans.


Floot also supports payments, custom domains, and integrations with external services. These capabilities help non-technical builders move beyond prototypes into applications with persistent data and ongoing business workflows.


### **Pricing Structure**


According to Floot's[live pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , its plans are:


- **Free ($0/month)** : 100 building actions per day, 3,000 starter AI credits for supported features, and a one-time $3 hosting allowance. Includes web building, previewing, and publishing.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 daily building actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, custom domains with one free domain, and priority support.
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 daily building actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25 monthly hosting allowance, unlimited mobile builds, and the features included in Pro.


Building through connected AI assistants uses the user's existing AI subscription and Floot building actions rather than separate Floot AI build credits for standard connector operations. AI credits apply to supported optional features, such as image generation, AI features running inside published apps, and building through Floot's own AI agent.


Hosting is metered separately. Pro and Power first use their monthly hosting allowances, followed by prepaid hosting credits. Free has no recurring monthly allowance, but new accounts receive a one-time $3 credit valid for one year. Automatic credit reloading is optional and disabled by default.


Floot is backed by Y Combinator's Summer 2025 batch and has a[4.8/5 G2 rating](https://www.g2.com/products/floot/reviews) .


### **What Sets Floot Apart**


Floot's[connector-based approach](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) allows people to build applications through supported AI assistants they already use. This separates the AI development workflow from the infrastructure needed to operate the finished application.


Users can build with Claude, Codex, Cursor, or compatible ChatGPT configurations while Floot provides the[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including databases, authentication, storage, and hosting. Connector permissions and supported operations vary by AI client.


Floot supports[mobile app publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) on every plan, with 2 monthly builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Floot builds, signs, and uploads apps to TestFlight and Google Play internal testing without requiring users to install Xcode or Android Studio. Apple developer accounts work with every Floot plan, while connecting Google Play requires Pro or Power. Users must complete their store listings and submit applications for review, and approval is not guaranteed.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable focuses on AI-generated web application interfaces, allowing users to create and refine designs through natural-language prompts. Lovable raised $400 million in Series C funding in August 2026 at a $13.3 billion valuation, following its $330 million Series B in December 2025.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable targets teams and individuals building web applications through natural-language prompts who want AI-assisted interface generation, managed backend options, and access to their source code.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **AI-powered UI generation** : Create and refine web application interfaces through natural-language prompts.
- **GitHub integration** : Connect repositories for source code access and version control.
- **Code ownership** : Access application code and explore self-hosting options.
- **Managed backend** : Lovable Cloud provides databases, authentication, and hosting.
- **Supabase integration** : Connect Supabase for additional backend requirements.


### **Considerations**


Lovable includes managed backend options, although teams may need additional configuration for specific services or integrations.


Its pricing uses credits for AI development operations and supported cloud services. The free plan includes a limited daily building allowance, while paid plans provide additional credits and capabilities.


Lovable focuses primarily on web applications rather than a dedicated native mobile app-building workflow.


For a more detailed comparison of development approaches, see[Floot vs Lovable](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) .


## **3. Replit**


Replit provides a browser-based development environment with AI Agent capabilities. It supports multiple programming languages and frameworks, combining traditional development tools with conversational AI application building.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit serves individual builders, developers, and technical teams who want AI-assisted development alongside direct access to code, debugging tools, and a complete browser-based IDE.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Browser-based IDE** : Access terminal tools, debugging, file management, and package management.
- **AI Agent** : Build, modify, and troubleshoot applications using natural-language prompts.
- **Multiple programming languages** : Supports Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and other languages.
- **Built-in hosting** : Deploy applications directly from the development environment.
- **Team collaboration** : Work together through shared development tools.


### **Considerations**


Replit provides developer-level controls through its IDE, while its AI Agent also supports application building without requiring users to write code manually.


The platform includes managed database and authentication services, with additional configuration options available for more technical requirements.


AI Agent usage is metered, and costs depend on the selected plan and development activity.


For a closer look at the infrastructure and development approaches, see[Floot vs Replit](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) .


## **4. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual programming platform with an extensive plugin ecosystem for extending application functionality. It supports web applications and native mobile app development through its visual development environment.


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble serves teams and individuals building complex web and mobile applications who want visual control over workflows, databases, and application behavior without relying on traditional source-code development.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Visual workflow builder** : Design interfaces and application logic using drag-and-drop tools.
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Access integrations for payments, analytics, authentication, and other services.
- **Built-in database** : Store and manage application data through a visual editor.
- **Native mobile builder** : Build iOS and Android applications on eligible plans.
- **Workflow customization** : Configure complex application behavior without traditional coding.


### **Considerations**


Bubble applications remain tied to the Bubble platform because it does not provide general source code export for independent self-hosting.


Users need to learn Bubble's visual workflow model to configure more complex application logic.


Its pricing includes workload-based usage, meaning operating costs depend partly on application activity and resource consumption.


## **5. Softr**


Softr specializes in creating client portals, internal tools, and business applications using built-in databases or external data sources such as Airtable, Google Sheets, and SQL databases. The platform reports serving more than one million teams globally.


### **Primary Focus**


Softr targets teams that need client-facing portals, internal dashboards, and operational applications built around existing data sources or new Softr Databases.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Data source integrations** : Connect Airtable, Google Sheets, Notion, HubSpot, and SQL databases.
- **Built-in databases** : Create applications using Softr Databases.
- **Ready-made templates** : Build client portals, dashboards, internal tools, and member directories.
- **User authentication** : Manage login access and user permissions.
- **Custom domains** : Connect branded domains on eligible paid plans.


### **Considerations**


Softr primarily produces web-based applications and mobile-friendly experiences rather than native iOS and Android applications for direct app store publishing.


The platform does not provide general application source code export for independent self-hosting.


Its free plan supports up to five app users. Higher plans provide additional capacity, permissions, and collaboration capabilities.


## **6. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow is a visual development platform that generates Flutter applications, making it an option for teams targeting mobile-first development with access to exported source code.


### **Primary Focus**


FlutterFlow serves teams building mobile-first applications that want visual development tools, source-code access, and the option to continue development with Flutter developers.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Flutter code export** : Generate Flutter and Dart source code for further development.
- **Visual UI builder** : Design application interfaces with drag-and-drop tools and real-time previews.
- **Mobile development** : Build applications for iOS and Android.
- **Backend integrations** : Connect Firebase and Supabase for databases and authentication.
- **Team collaboration** : Access version-control and collaborative development features on eligible plans.


### **Considerations**


FlutterFlow commonly relies on Firebase, Supabase, or other backend services for databases and authentication, which may require additional setup.


The platform emphasizes Flutter-based development, making it suitable for teams comfortable with that technology.


Exported projects use Flutter and Dart, so further development requires familiarity with the Flutter technology stack.


## **7. Base44**


Base44 offers an AI app-building platform with managed backend services, targeting users who want to create applications through natural-language prompts with limited manual configuration. Wix acquired Base44 in June 2025.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 targets beginners, entrepreneurs, and business teams seeking conversational AI application building with managed backend services and minimal initial configuration.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Conversational AI building** : Generate applications using natural-language descriptions.
- **Managed backend** : Access built-in database and authentication services.
- **Beginner-friendly setup** : Build applications with limited manual infrastructure configuration.
- **Code export** : Download application source code on eligible plans.
- **GitHub integration** : Connect repositories for source code management.


### **Considerations**


Base44 supports source code export and GitHub integration, but exported applications may retain dependencies on Base44's managed backend services.


Moving an exported application to independent infrastructure can require replacing database, authentication, and other platform-specific services.


For additional context about full-stack infrastructure and code portability, see[Floot vs Base44](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **8. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, host, and publish websites and lightweight web applications directly through ChatGPT. It supports interactive dashboards, internal tools, and other web experiences without requiring a separate deployment workflow.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites serves ChatGPT users who want to create and publish websites, dashboards, and lightweight applications without managing a separate deployment environment.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **Conversational building** : Create and refine websites and lightweight web applications through ChatGPT.
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish projects using shareable URLs and supported custom domains.
- **Data storage** : Store supported application data and uploaded files.
- **Authentication** : Manage site access through available sign-in and access-control options.
- **Connected services** : Access supported integrations based on workspace permissions and settings.


### **Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites is designed for hosted web experiences rather than native iOS and Android app store publishing.


Some frameworks, databases, background services, and hosting configurations may not be supported because of runtime limitations.


Building and editing Sites count toward Codex usage, while hosting and storage have separate usage limits determined by the applicable ChatGPT plan.


## **Why Floot Leads for Full-Stack AI App Building**


For builders evaluating Zite alternatives, Floot offers a full-stack application development option that combines AI assistant workflows with managed infrastructure. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports building through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, while Floot handles the backend services required to run and publish applications.


This approach is particularly relevant for non-technical founders and business operators who want applications with user accounts, persistent data, and business workflows without independently configuring multiple backend services.


Floot provides several capabilities for building and managing working applications:


- **AI-assisted development** : Create, edit, debug, and publish applications through supported connected AI assistants, depending on available connector permissions.
- **Managed infrastructure** : Use[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) including PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, transactional email, and hosting.
- **Mobile development options** : Use[Floot's mobile workflows](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) to create iOS and Android builds on any plan, with cloud-based packaging and supported testing-track uploads.
- **Code ownership and export** : Retain ownership of code, data, and intellectual property, with[ZIP exports](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) available on paid plans for independent deployment and further customization.
- **SEO capabilities** : Use[SEO tools](https://floot.com/en/seo) such as server-side pre-rendering, sitemap generation, metadata management, and custom domain support.
- **Usage-based infrastructure** : Monitor hosting consumption through[hosting controls](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/hosting) , with monthly allowances on paid plans and prepaid credit for additional usage.


For founders, operators, and business owners who already use supported AI assistants, Floot provides a practical path from an application idea to a published full-stack product. The[Floot showcase](https://floot.com/en/showcase) includes community-built projects, while the[current pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) page explains the available plans and hosting allowances.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the main difference between Floot and Zite for AI app building?**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector for supported AI assistants, combining AI-driven development with managed databases, authentication, storage, and hosting. Zite emphasizes business workflow applications with unlimited users and a visual workflow editor. Its Business plan also advertises building with an external AI assistant, although the specific workflow and available operations depend on its supported integrations. Floot also provides project ZIP exports on paid plans and iOS and Android mobile builds across all three plans, while Zite focuses on hosted web applications without general source code export. Learn more about Floot's[connector workflow](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) .


### **Can existing ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions be used to build apps with these platforms?**


Yes. Floot allows users to[create and manage applications](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Standard connector-based building uses the existing AI subscription alongside Floot's daily building action allowances. Separate Floot AI credits are not generally required for those operations, although optional image generation and other Floot AI services may consume credits. Other platforms offer different AI integrations, usage allowances, and billing arrangements. For Floot, available actions depend on the connected client's permissions and capabilities.


### **Which Zite alternatives support mobile app development?**


Floot, FlutterFlow, and Bubble provide different approaches to[mobile app development](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) . Floot packages web applications into installable iOS and Android apps, with 2 monthly builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. FlutterFlow generates Flutter applications, while Bubble offers native mobile development. Floot handles cloud-based builds without requiring local Xcode or Android Studio. App-store publishing requires separate developer accounts, and approval is not guaranteed.


### **Do any of these platforms offer code export for self-hosting?**


Yes. Floot, Lovable, FlutterFlow, Replit, and Base44 provide different forms of code access or export. Floot allows users to download complete project source code as ZIP files on paid plans. Lovable provides source code access through GitHub, FlutterFlow exports Flutter and Dart code, and Replit provides access through its development environment. Base44 also supports code export, but its managed backend dependencies may require additional migration work. Zite, Bubble, and Softr do not provide general application code exports for independent self-hosting. Floot's[self-hosting guide](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) explains code and database export, alongside the infrastructure changes needed when moving away from managed hosting.


### **How do pricing models compare between these AI app builders?**


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with Pro at $25/month and Power at $100/month. Zite Pro costs $25/month with monthly billing, or $20/month billed annually, Lovable Pro at $25/month, and Replit Core at $20/month. Bubble Web Starter starts at $32/month billed annually, Softr Basic at $25/month, and FlutterFlow Basic at $39/month. ChatGPT Sites is available through eligible ChatGPT subscriptions. Actual costs depend on AI usage, hosting, and billing terms. See Floot pricing for current plans and allowances.
